title: Authority Questioned and Teaching in the Temple

questions.question: As Jesus was teaching the people in the temple and preaching the gospel, the chief priests, scribes, and elders confronted Him. What did they ask Him?
options: "Tell us by what authority you do these things, or who it is that gave you this authority." (Luke 20:2)
"When will you present yourself fully to Pilate?"
"Why have you torn down the tables of our commerce?"
"How can you claim to be the Son of David without an army?"
questions.correctAnswer: "Tell us by what authority you do these things, or who it is that gave you this authority." (Luke 20:2)
questions.explanation: Luke 20:2 (ESV): "and said to him, 'Tell us by what authority you do these things, or who it is that gave you this authority.'"

questions.question: Jesus countered their question with one of His own regarding the baptism of John: "Was it from heaven, or from man?" Why did they reason among themselves not to say "From heaven"?
options: They reasoned, "If we say, 'From heaven,' he will say, 'Why did you not believe him?'"
They reasoned, "Because we know John was simply a madman in the desert."
They reasoned, "Because admitting so would anger Herod the Tetrarch."
They feared angels would strike them instantly dead for lying.
questions.correctAnswer: They reasoned, "If we say, 'From heaven,' he will say, 'Why did you not believe him?'"
questions.explanation: Luke 20:5 (ESV): "And they discussed it with one another, saying, 'If we say, "From heaven," he will say, "Why did you not believe him?"'"

questions.question: Why did the religious leaders decide not to say John's baptism was "from man"?
options: "All the people will stone us to death, for they are convinced that John was a prophet."
"We will be stripped of our priestly garments in disgrace."
"The Roman guards will arrest us for stirring up a riot entirely."
"Jesus easily defeats such poor theological arguments always."
questions.correctAnswer: "All the people will stone us to death, for they are convinced that John was a prophet."
questions.explanation: Luke 20:6 (ESV): "But if we say, 'From man,' all the people will stone us to death, for they are convinced that John was a prophet."

questions.question: In the Parable of the Wicked Tenants, what did the tenants do to the three different servants sent by the owner to get a share of the fruit?
options: They beat them, treated them shamefully, wounded them, and cast them out empty-handed
They murdered them entirely and buried them amidst the vines
They bribed them heavily with silver to keep quiet forever
They locked them in the stone watchtower to starve
questions.correctAnswer: They beat them, treated them shamefully, wounded them, and cast them out empty-handed
questions.explanation: Luke 20:10-12 details that they beat the first, beat and treated the second shamefully, and wounded and cast out the third.

questions.question: When the owner finally sent his beloved son, saying "Perhaps they will respect him," what was the reasoning of the tenants when they saw the son?
options: "This is the heir. Let us kill him, so that the inheritance may be ours."
"The master finally comes! Let us appease him with wine."
"We will hold him for ransom and take the land legally."
"We must flee entirely, for justice has arrived!"
questions.correctAnswer: "This is the heir. Let us kill him, so that the inheritance may be ours."
questions.explanation: Luke 20:14 (ESV): "But when the tenants saw him, they said to themselves, 'This is the heir. Let us kill him, so that the inheritance may be ours.'"

questions.question: What did the people say when Jesus stated the master will come, destroy those tenants, and give the vineyard to others?
options: "Surely not!"
"Let his will be done!"
"A harsh master indeed!"
"They brought it perfectly upon themselves!"
questions.explanation: Luke 20:16 (ESV): "He will come and destroy those tenants and give the vineyard to others. When they heard this, they said, 'Surely not!'"

questions.question: Looking directly at them, Jesus quoted Scripture: "The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone." What did He say happens to everyone who falls on that stone?
options: They will be broken to pieces
They will be swallowed into the earth
They will be blinded by its brilliance
They will be ground into fine sand immediately
questions.correctAnswer: They will be broken to pieces
questions.explanation: Luke 20:18 (ESV): "Everyone who falls on that stone will be broken to pieces, and when it falls on anyone, it will crush him."

questions.question: The scribes and chief priests sought to lay hands on Him that very hour but feared the people. They watched Him and sent spies, pretending to be sincere, in order to catch Him in something He said, so they could deliver Him over to the authority of whom?
options: The governor
The high priest entirely
The Herodian courts
The Sanhedrin judges
questions.explanation: Luke 20:20 (ESV): "...so as to deliver him up to the authority and jurisdiction of the governor."

questions.question: The spies tried to trap Him by asking: "Is it lawful for us to give tribute to Caesar, or not?" What specifically did Jesus ask them to show Him?
options: A denarius
A gold talent
A shekel of the sanctuary
Two copper coins
questions.explanation: Luke 20:24 (ESV): "Show me a denarius. Whose likeness and inscription does it have?"

questions.question: How did Jesus silence their trap about paying taxes to Caesar?
options: "Then render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's."
"Keep the silver for yourselves, and give gold to the king."
"Whatever belongs to Rome, throw it back into the sea."
"The tribute is an abomination, but you must suffer in peace."
questions.correctAnswer: "Then render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's."
questions.explanation: Luke 20:25 (ESV): "He said to them, 'Then render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's.'"

questions.question: There came to Him some Sadducees, those who deny that there is a resurrection. They posed a scenario about seven brothers who married the same woman sequentially, and all died childless. Whose wife will she be in the resurrection? How did Jesus describe those considered worthy of the resurrection from the dead?
options: They neither marry nor are given in marriage, for they are equal to angels and are sons of God
She is restored solely to the first brother permanently
They live separate lives, no longer needing anyone
She may finally choose which brother she loved the most
questions.correctAnswer: They neither marry nor are given in marriage, for they are equal to angels and are sons of God
questions.explanation: Luke 20:35-36 (ESV): "but those who are considered worthy to attain to that age and to the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage, for they cannot die anymore, because they are equal to angels..."

questions.question: To prove the dead are raised, Jesus recalled Moses at the bush, where the Lord is called the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Jesus declared: "Now he is not God of the dead, but of the living, for..."?
options: "...all live to him."
"...their spirits dance before his throne in heaven."
"...they wander Paradise awaiting the final trumpet."
"...He preserves their bones intact in the dust."
questions.explanation: Luke 20:38 (ESV): "Now he is not God of the dead, but of the living, for all live to him."

questions.question: After Jesus answered the Sadducees so well, some of the scribes answered, "Teacher, you have spoken well." What did they no longer dare to do?
options: They no longer dared to ask him any question
They no longer dared to arrest him in public openly
They no longer dared to attend the Passover feast
They no longer dared to sit near the temple treasury
questions.correctAnswer: They no longer dared to ask him any question
questions.explanation: Luke 20:40 (ESV): "For they no longer dared to ask him any question."

questions.question: Jesus asked them a question about the Christ. He quoted David from the Book of Psalms: "The Lord said to my Lord, 'Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool.'" What contradiction was Jesus pointing out?
options: "David thus calls him Lord, so how is he his son?"
"David killed Goliath, yet the Christ claims peace; how is this possible?"
"The Lord does not need a footstool, so why does David claim this?"
"How can a man sit at the right hand of Spirit?"
questions.correctAnswer: "David thus calls him Lord, so how is he his son?"
questions.explanation: Luke 20:44 (ESV): "David thus calls him Lord, so how is he his son?"

questions.question: In the hearing of all the people, Jesus warned His disciples to beware of the scribes. Which of the following is NOT one of the things He accused the scribes of doing?
options: Drinking wine mixed with myrrh secretly in the cellars
Walking around in long robes and loving greetings in the marketplaces
Devouring widows' houses
For a pretense making long prayers
questions.correctAnswer: Drinking wine mixed with myrrh secretly in the cellars
questions.explanation: Luke 20:46-47 (ESV): "Beware of the scribes, who like to walk around in long robes, and love greetings in the marketplaces... who devour widows' houses and for a pretense make long prayers."

key_verse_text: He said to them, "Then render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's."
